question: An international judicial body, ensuring protection of rights, was established by a continental union in a West African capital in the sixth month of a year in the late 1990s. This body selects its members from individuals with recognized scholarly abilities. One person exemplifying such abilities, though from a different context, is a polyglot and educator from an Eastern European country specializing in a specific East Asian language. He is noted for authoring several influential books on this language. One of his key publications, a comprehensive guide for adult learners of this language, earned significant praise. This particular guide was honored at a prominent annual cultural gathering dedicated to literature and publishing. This gathering, the largest of its kind in its nation, has been held every autumn since the mid-1990s in the same city where the aforementioned educator was born. This city, known for its literary event, also hosts an athletic organization. This sports club, which once saw its best players transfer to a local competitor, later achieved a notable stage in a national non-professional knockout competition. That specific national knockout competition, involving non-professional teams, had this particular iteration as the first one managed by a newly formed national amateur sports association. What was the sequential number of this annual competition season?

Consider a linguistic technique for studying language evolution by comparing features of related languages to extrapolate their shared ancestor, a method significantly advanced by a 19th-century scholar also known for his collection of folk tales. This technique is applied to poorly attested ancient languages, like one spoken in a historical southeastern European region which, according to one theory, shares affinities with a specific northern branch of its overarching language family. This northern branch (one prominent member first appearing in print via a religious instructional text in the mid-1500s) diverged from a common proto-language, shared with a major eastern European language group. This proto-language, existing during the early medieval period, had its accentual system shaped by phonetic laws. One such law, named after two specialists, shifted accents rightward in fixed-accent words. However, this law was blocked in mobile stress words due to another principle affecting the root's tone in such paradigms. What is the full name of the linguist, from a nation famed for its iconic capital city landmark, after whom this latter principle is named?

An electoral zone in a northern UK city, defined in the late 19th century, saw its city become part of a larger administrative unit in the mid-1970s due to a specific law. This larger unit, named after a mountain range and lasting about two decades, was later divided into unitary authorities. Its existence as a type of 'region' is documented in governmental organization chronicles, which also outline how the country is currently divided. The current system involves 'council areas' that superseded older, historically significant 'shire'-like territories. These 'shire'-like territories, established for justice in medieval times, ceased to be used for local administration due to parliamentary legislation enacted in a year three years into the 1970s. This legislation radically reformed local governance, replacing old structures with a two-tier system. On what date (day, month, year) did this act become operative?

What is the name of the country where a gold medalist at the FIS Nordic World Ski Championships held in Cortina d'Ampezzo was born, given that the championships did not have participants from Finland or Norway?

What is the name of the publisher that reissued in 2009 a book published in 1851, which was co-authored, advocated for atheistic naturalism, systematically explores phrenology and mesmerism, and was controversial for doing so?

What is the name of the person who was elected as the chief executive of an area in 1998, served until 2007, who was responsible for implementing a law signed by Elpidio Quirino with an effective date of June 16, 1948, which established that area by segregating territory from Zamboanga City, and which later became a province?
